newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BT not interested in Telstra stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BT not interested in Telstra stake.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) said it would not be interested in buying a stake in Australia's state-owned Telstra Corp when it is privatised, BT deputy chief executive Alan Rudge said in a television interview broadcast on Sunday.

"If we look at the Telstra opportunity, I would say it's unlikely and it's unlikely because the conditions dictate that we could have anything up to five percent of Telstra," Rudge told the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
"Those kind of very low level equity investments are not something we find very attractive," he said.
In early December, the conservative Australian government won approval to sell a third of Telstra Corp.
But the privatisation legislation limits foreign investors to 11.7 percent of Telstra and no individual foreigner will be able to buy more than five percent.
The government plans to raise about A$8 billion through the sale, which is not expected to take place until the final quarter of calendar 1997.
Telstra, Australia's largest telecommunications group, posted a 31.5 percent rise in net profit to A$2.30 billion for the year to June 30, 1996.
Rudge said, however, that BT would consider a significant investment in Australia's second largest telecommunications group, Optus, if the opportunity came along.
"I don't know that there is one at the moment of significant scale, but we would consider it," he said.

The privately owned and unlisted Optus, which is 25 percent owned by Mayne Nickless Ltd, wants to float later this year, but is currently embroiled in a legal dispute with the Seven Network which has put those float plans on hold.
Foreigners are currently limited to 49 percent of Optus, which is owned 24.5 percent each by BellSouth Corp and Cable and Wireless Plc.
BT is seen unlikely to be offered a significant stake while Cable and Wireless is a major shareholder.
